references.shows: The YFG-811 and YFG-812 show the tall straight bass joint, parallel shorter wing joint and low boot in a neutral front view.
Anatomy overview and illustrated instrument variants: Two parallel wooden tube runs joined at the boot. Long wing and bass joints.
Photographic reference collection for bassoon: compare long wing and bass joints and upward open bell. Select the variant described in notes.

silhouette: A tall folded wooden woodwind held diagonally upright, with a narrow metal crook projecting toward the player.
features: Two parallel wooden tube runs joined at the boot
Curved metal bocal ending in a small double reed
Silver keywork on the wooden body
iconFeatures: Tall doubled tube and curved bocal in upright playing pose
avoid: A single straight clarinet or a saxophone
Brand logos, wordmarks and decorative text that obscure the instrument anatomy
notes: The YFG-811 and YFG-812 photographs guide the proportions of the two parallel wooden runs and boot. The artwork tilts the full instrument into its upright playing pose.

geometry.proportions: The tall, narrow body has two parallel legs joined at the boot; the bell rises higher.
geometry.partLayout: The metal bocal bends away from the wing joint toward its reed. Preserve the low boot and the gap between bocal and bell.
